tags.chapter_name: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

question.text: A ball with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> collides with another identical ball at rest. After the collision, the direction of each ball makes an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with the original direction. If the ratio of velocities of the balls after the collision is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>y</mi></math>, then what is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>?

solution.text:
From conservation of momentum along y-axis.

P→iy=P→fy

0+0=mv1sin30°j^+mv2sin30°-j^

mv2sin30°=mv1sin30°

v2=v1 or v1v2=1
